claims.text: The baseline HfMoTaTiZr is a fully dense, as-cast alloy.
The baseline HfMoTaTiZr density is approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength of approximately 1600 MPa.
HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength of approximately 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
Laser powder bed fusion or electron beam melting can fabricate HfMoTaTiZr lattices with 150–300 μm struts, 1–3 mm cells, and 10–20% open space.
Additive fabrication of the proposed lattice can introduce site-specific porosity without altering the nominal HfMoTaTiZr composition.
A continuous, interconnected network of dense HfMoTaTiZr struts will support external loads.
Engineered porosity will reduce total part mass and bulk density.
The lattice struts will retain the as-cast alloy's BCC-based microstructure.
The retained microstructure in the struts will preserve the alloy's high-temperature strength.
Removing material from low-stress regions will lower density without significantly reducing load-bearing capacity.
Introducing the proposed lattice will not significantly reduce phase stability.
The lattice part will have a bulk density below 9.5 g/cm³.
The lattice part will retain a room-temperature yield strength of at least 1500 MPa.
The lattice part will retain a yield strength of at least 800 MPa at 1000 °C.
The additive process can be kept consistent with maintaining a single-phase BCC microstructure in the struts.
Struts thinner than 100 μm risk failing to meet the specified strength targets.
Void volume above 30% risks failing to meet the specified strength targets.
Prior testing demonstrates strong elevated-temperature mechanical performance in dense HfMoTaTiZr-related refractory alloys.
The effect of the proposed lattice on local stress distributions and mechanical retention is unproven.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says the lattice will use and retain an as-cast microstructure, but the proposed laser- or electron-beam additive process remelts and resolidifies pre-alloyed feedstock. The resulting struts are additively manufactured rather than as-cast, so microstructural retention is internally inconsistent unless equivalence is experimentally demonstrated.
